assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clear, well-bounded invention: a unipolar semiconductor laser whose emission wavelength is set by engineered quantum-well layer thicknesses rather than the bandgap, demonstrated in 1994. It opened the mid-infrared and terahertz regimes, is in commercial use for trace-gas sensing and spectroscopy, and rests on epitaxial growth precision and band-structure engineering that I recognise as hard materials physics. It fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion well.
assessment.attribution: Capasso led the conception and the Bell Labs team; Faist carried out the first demonstration and later room-temperature and continuous-wave work; Cho's molecular-beam-epitaxy growth made the layered structures possible. Other Bell Labs co-authors (e.g. Sirtori, Hutchinson, Sivco) are not in the credited list, so a three-person configuration omits some team members. The Kazarinov-Suris 1971 proposal is an earlier theoretical antecedent that complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of independent development, broad replication, room-temperature continuous-wave operation and wide application make this mature and timely.
uncertainties: Whether Cho's growth role is a decisive contribution or an enabling technique relative to Capasso and Faist.
The Kazarinov-Suris proposal and omitted Bell Labs co-inventors complicate priority.
My recollection of the detailed team roles has not been independently checked here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's implementation and refinement of strontium clocks, reaches fractional uncertainty near 1e-18. This is a definable invention with great precision-measurement value, relevance to a possible redefinition of the second, and demonstrated use in relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept in 2001-2003 and Ye brought the systems to record accuracy. A two-person prize is clean. Contributions from Hall and Hänsch (already honoured in 2005), Ludlow, Bloom and Schiller or Lemonde-type groups, and the Wineland ion clocks are related but not in the credited set; I would treat them as context.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have reproduced 1e-18-level performance and the field is stable, though the redefinition of the second is still pending.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views lattice clocks as sufficiently distinct from earlier clock-related prizes.
Priority and shared credit with other optical-lattice and ion-clock groups is not fully resolved in the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection of single nitrogen-vacancy centres and their coherent control at room temperature is a clear experimental breakthrough that created solid-state spin qubits and nanoscale quantum sensing. NV sensing now reaches magnetometry, thermometry and bio-imaging, and the defect physics sits naturally close to my interest in point defects, imaging and spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group reported single-NV optical detection in 1997 and Jelezko and Wrachtrup demonstrated coherent control around 2004. Lukin and others contributed important theory and applications such as sensing proposals, but the original experimental discovery is best credited to the two Stuttgart researchers. Dutt, Hanson and Awschalom-type contributions in related directions could argue for a broader configuration.
assessment.maturity: Replicated worldwide, with practical sensing devices and a stable interpretation, so it is mature.
uncertainties: Whether Lukin's sensing and quantum-register proposals should displace one experimentalist.
Overlap with the separate spin-photon-interface candidate and Awschalom-type contributions not credited here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene near a magic angle, followed by the 2018 observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states, opened moiré quantum materials as a tunable platform for correlated physics. Originality and impact are high and the field is huge.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group did the decisive 2018 experiments with Cao and Fatemi, who are not credited, and Yuan Cao as first author is notable. Credit for the experiment also involves other groups (e.g. Dean, Young, Yazdani, Efetov) whose independent confirmation matters. A fair configuration exists but is debatable.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across many groups is strong, but the interpretation of the superconducting mechanism remains open, and the field is still evolving, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The superconducting mechanism is unresolved.
Whether credit should rest with the experimental team leader or include first-author trainees outside the credited list.
Possible overlap with moiré fractional quantum anomalous Hall candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the time-reversal-invariant quantum spin Hall state and Z2 topological classification, followed by experimental realisation in HgTe wells, established topological insulators as a major paradigm of condensed matter. Impact on materials and spectroscopy (ARPES) is lasting, and the field is well established.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theory; Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted HgTe, and Molenkamp's group observed the effect in 2007; Hasan and others did 3D Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 experiments. Limiting to three names forces omission of Zhang, Hasan, Fu, Moore, Balents and Roy, which is a genuine allocation problem. Zhang is deceased, which also affects configuration.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and long, stable interpretation make it mature, though recognition may have been delayed by credit disputes.
uncertainties: Substantial credit conflict: Zhang's role in the HgTe prediction and Hasan's 3D results versus the three credited names.
Whether the 2D or 3D discovery should be the prized topic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of a high-mobility two-dimensional electron gas at the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interface in 2004, followed by interface superconductivity and electric-field control, demonstrated that oxide interfaces create new electronic phases. The topic is important in correlated-electron materials and relies on atomic-scale interface characterisation including electron microscopy and spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Ohtomo and Hwang reported the interface 2DEG; Mannhart's group contributed superconductivity and gate control and the polar-discontinuity picture, along with Triscone and others not credited. Hwang and Ohtomo are clearest for the original discovery.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated, but the origin of the carriers (polar catastrophe versus oxygen vacancies and intermixing) has been debated for years and is still not fully settled. I note that my own published work touches oxygen vacancies and interfaces in this system, so I should be cautious and declare a possible bias; that is why I do not rank it higher.
uncertainties: Disputed role of oxygen vacancies and cation intermixing versus intrinsic polar doping.
Possible bias from my own research connection to this materials system.
Whether Mannhart's contribution is on the same level as Ohtomo and Hwang.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling to superconducting circuits and underpins superconducting quantum processors and dispersive qubit readout. It is conceptually clear and widely used, though recent prizes in superconducting quantum circuits may reduce room for a further award in this area.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal; Wallraff and Schoelkopf's group demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Four credited names exceed the three-person limit, so Blais or another must be excluded, which is a real allocation difficulty. Closely related transmon work by Schoelkopf's group adds to the case.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and replicated, with ongoing technological impact.
uncertainties: Overlap with recently recognised superconducting-circuit work may make this look redundant.
Excluding Blais from the three-person limit is contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-halide perovskites reached high solar-cell efficiencies with remarkable speed and have spurred wide materials physics work on defect tolerance, ion migration and optoelectronics. The impact is large, but the discovery is as much a materials and device development as a single physical discovery.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell in 2009 (with Kojima, who is not credited); Park's 2011-2012 work and Snaith's 2012 efforts brought the solid-state breakthrough, with Grätzel and others also contributing. Credit is contested and the three-name list omits some central contributors, which weakens attribution.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are confirmed independently, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and scaling remain unresolved, which suggests recognition may be premature for the physics prize.
uncertainties: Contested credit and omission of Kojima and others.
Operational stability is unresolved.
Whether it is a physics discovery rather than a device optimisation.
